text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad called on South Korea on Wednesday to buy more Malaysian goods and invest more in his country, saying he was disappointed with the level of trade between the two sides.
The official Bernama news agency quoted Mahathir as saying in talks with visiting South Korean President Kim Young-sam that Seoul seemed "cold" to the idea of increasing investment.

"Dr Mahathir was also dissatisfied with the balance of trade between the two countries and asked South Korea to buy more Malaysian raw materials directly and not through third countries," Bernama quoted Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi as telling a media briefing on the talks.
"Even their proposed investments in Malaysia are not big enough and that is the message the Prime Minister conveyed to President Kim," Abdullah said.
Officials said bilateral trade totalled 11.07 billion ringgit ($4.4 billion) in 1995 and was 58 percent in South Korea's favour.
Mahathir also told Kim if South Korea expanded business in Malaysia, it should do so in non labour-intensive sectors because Kuala Lumpur was phasing out such industries, Abdullah said.
"At the policy level, the two leaders expressed hope that their respective business communities would overcome whatever problems faced in good spirit," Abdullah said.

Kim, who arrived on Tuesday for a three-day visit, was accompanied by South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha, Trade, Industry and Energy Minister Park Jae-yoon and South Korean ambassador to Malaysia Jhung Kyung-yil.
Mahathir was joined by Abdullah and Malaysia's Minister of International Trade and Industry Rafidah Aziz.
